content:
The observatory forecasts that today's outdoor maximum temperature will be 34 degrees, approaching the 2022 record of 34.9 degrees for the hottest "Great Heat" day, about 4 degrees higher than last year's "Great Heat".

The observatory has continued to issue the Very Hot Weather Warning, forecasting that today will be generally fine, but with showers in some areas from morning to noon, with daytime temperatures being extremely hot. Additionally, a subtropical high-pressure ridge is bringing clear weather to Hong Kong, but coastal areas will also be affected by showers.

The heatwave caused by the "Great Heat" has made Hong Kong's streets as stifling as an oven, with a thermometer at Mong Kok Macpherson Playground recording a high of 40.8 degrees.

In the past, the highest maximum temperature on the "Great Heat" was 34.9 degrees in 2022, and the lowest was 22.2 degrees in 1965.

Additionally, the highest average relative humidity recorded on the "Great Heat" in past years was 96% in 1994, with the highest total rainfall of 195.1 millimetres, while the lowest average relative humidity was 70% in 1968.
